issues.description: SlingScriptResolverImpl.findScript — a separate attacker-reachable entry point that the official fix guards with isInvalidPath — is left completely unpatched, so that path to the sink remains vulnerable.

The absolute-path resourceType branch of SlingServletResolver.resolveServletInternal (scriptNameOrResourceType.charAt(0)=='/') bypasses the collectors entirely and is not covered by the isContained checks.

NamedScriptResourceCollector's isContained operates on the normalized string, not the resolved resource path; a multi-dot segment ('...') that ResourceUtil.normalize does not collapse (precisely what the official isInvalidPath targets) can stay within the base prefix and slip through.
NamedScriptResourceCollectorTest extends HelperTestBase with an un-annotated test method (JUnit3/4 style mismatch); it may silently not execute, giving false confidence in coverage.

result.root_cause: The resolver appends caller-controlled segments (script name, selectors, resource type) to a trusted base path and resolves the result without verifying that the canonicalized path stays inside the allowed script tree, permitting traversal to arbitrary scripts.
result.summary: Our patch blocks the observed POV and applies a legitimate canonicalize-then-contain guard (ResourceUtil.normalize + isContained) inside the two AbstractResourceCollector subclasses, which is the right CWE-022 primitive for the collector-driven resolution flow. However it fixes a different location than the official reference and leaves gaps: the SlingScriptResolverImpl.findScript entry point and the absolute-path resourceType branch are untouched, and one branch checks the normalized string rather than the resolved resource path, so a multi-dot ('...') segment that the official isInvalidPath specifically rejects may slip through. It is a weaker subset of the official fix — good for the reported trigger but not demonstrably closing the whole class.
